title: regrain(), regrain_history() and a hand regrain_step copy and swap through a REPEATABLE READ caller's snapshot, dropping rows committed after it
the readers of a retirement mark vouch for it without the dispatch record, so the archive step records a hand-detached table as covered and retention drops it once attached back
archive._owned_key claims key bases as raw text, so under MinIO's leading-slash normalisation a namesake's chunk overwrites the dropped table's only copy
_regrain_copy_make's LIKE ... INCLUDING CONSTRAINTS validates a NOT VALID CHECK on the copy, so a violating row wedges the regrain until regrain_cancel
adopt_partition judges attachment and the pending flag through the caller's transaction snapshot, before and after its lock, and does not refuse a stricter isolation level
_snapshot_wait judges a snapshot by the cluster-wide backend_xmin, so a transaction open in another database defers every swap and the refusal names an innocent pid
_over_retired_chunks reads a legacy offset-less retired ledger bound in the caller's session TimeZone
check_time_monotonic casts a naive timestamp column to timestamptz in the caller's session TimeZone
from_hypertable_copy resolves the key's constraint by conindid alone, so an incoming foreign key on the key pre-builds the wrong index and the key is built twice
_surface_prepare drops a shape-changed surface function and recreates it, losing the operator's grants the install's header promises to keep
_from_hypertable_check_arguments does not ask transmute's mixed month-and-duration step rule before the copy and swap
archive.configure accepts an endpoint with a trailing slash, after which every signed request addresses //bucket/key and is refused
transmute's resume checks the claim's column and grid but not the text_time encoding, so a re-run with another encoding fails raw in the cutover
_regrain_capture_names resolves the recorded capture function only in the delta's current schema, so untransmute and uninstall leave it behind after the delta is moved
retain_disown's remedy, in the log row and the reference, says to drop the table by hand and omits the pgpm.part row that then wedges retention
_transmute_refuse_staging_squatter hard-codes a drop table remedy whatever kind of relation holds the staging name
_transmute_refuse_child_holders accepts any time label of the kind, so an operator's table at a label the grid could never mint blocks the conversion
the reference says a naive timestamp column holding wall time east of UTC runs on an hourly grid, but the frontier skew refusal stops it unless p_force_frontier is passed
_time_unit_breach flags a date anchor off midnight for a whole-month step whose bounds all land at midnight: the upgrade warns and set_regrain refuses for a false reason
CHANGELOG.md's #1161 bullet carries a stale duplicated tail saying set_regrain refuses a run past the lock budget, where it warns
check_quoted_splices.py never reads a FOR loop's target as an assignment and never reads a body dollar-quoted with a tag other than $$
check_archive_object_keys.py misses a prefix bound as an EXECUTE ... USING argument, renamed through a FROM item or handed by position to a helper
bench/ci_runs_lint_jobs.sh accepts test.sh's ci on the spelling of its lint call and never requires that ci fails when the lint track fails
bench/run_fh.sh calls from_hypertable_cutover with p_regrain_batch, a parameter it does not have, so every documented hypertable benchmark run dies after its copy
bench/run.sh's conservation gate counts history rows where its own comment and the README promise every row is still present
tests/timescale/db/65 and 66 look for leftover scratch records under the new partitioned tables' oids, not the dropped hypertables' oids the records carry
tests/archive/db/08, 16 and 44 judge the objects they wrote back by line count, size or a PAR1 prefix, not by identity with the chunk's rows
tests/72's row-level-security check asks only the role the policy names, so a policy replayed to every role passes
tests/27 asserts that untransmute preserves all rows by a count of 100 over a fixture whose rows can be told apart
check_archive_child_by_oid.py's rule 1 refuses a run-time name cast to regclass only as )::regclass, not ::pg_catalog.regclass, CAST(... AS regclass) or regclass(...)
stop_check.py judges the stopping thresholds on the record header's two-decimal figures, so 0.696 precision, 0.304 fell or 0.897 coverage read as met
pass_metrics.py counts a candidate with no verdict, or an unknown verdict string, as fell, inflating the fell rate the stopping criteria read
decisions_queue.py skips a malformed line instead of refusing it, so an indented, star-bulleted or lower-case BLOCKING entry is never read and the loop continues
